airport: An airport features large expanses of smooth gray runway strips with clear white markings, adjacent terminal buildings, and expansive aprons with parked aircraft, distinguishing it from the uniform gray grid of parking lots, the regular crop patterns of farmland, the dense building clusters of urban centers, and the linear railway tracks of railway stations.
bareland: Bareland presents a broad, flat expanse of uniform light brown or tan soil with a smooth fine-grained texture and no visible vegetation or structures, distinguishing it from the vast uniform sandy tones of desert, the rugged rocky terrain of mountains, the regular geometric crop patterns of farmland, and the flat paved surfaces of industrial zones.
baseballfield: A baseball field displays a distinctive fan-shaped green outfield with a diamond-shaped dirt infield, surrounding circular arc boundary, and adjacent rectangular parking areas, distinguishing it from the oval or rectangular enclosed structure of stadiums, the open green lawns of parks, the rectangular courts of playgrounds, and the smooth water surfaces of ponds.
beach: A beach appears as a broad, smooth expanse of fine light tan sand with a gentle natural transition to water, often with subtle wave patterns along the shoreline, distinguishing it from the sinuous dark water ribbon of rivers, the vast uniform dry sand of deserts, the developed shoreline of resorts, and the calm enclosed water of ponds.
bridge: A bridge appears as a linear elevated structure crossing perpendicularly over a dark water body, with visible support pillars and shadow patterns on the water surface below, distinguishing it from the flowing dark water of rivers, the elongated elevated structure of viaducts, the flat gray surfaces of parking lots, and the built-up structures of industrial areas.
center: An urban center displays a dense cluster of tall, varied-size rectangular buildings with complex rooftop structures, narrow street grids, and minimal green space, distinguishing it from the large oval structures of stadiums, the distinctive spired or cross-shaped rooftops of churches, the uniform commercial blocks of commercial zones, and the expansive paved areas of parking lots.
church: A church features a distinctive rectangular building with a prominent tall steeple or spire, often cross-shaped floor plan visible from above, surrounded by small parking areas and open space, distinguishing it from the dense building clusters of urban centers, the large flat parking surfaces nearby, the rectangular layouts of schools, and the open plazas of squares.
commercial: Commercial areas display dense clusters of medium-to-large rectangular buildings with flat rooftops, extensive paved parking lots between structures, and regular street grids, distinguishing them from the dense tall buildings of urban centers, the large factory buildings of industrial zones, the uniform gray parking surfaces, and the green open spaces of parks.
denseresidential: Dense residential areas show tightly packed small rectangular rooftops with minimal spacing, narrow winding streets, and very limited green space between buildings, distinguishing them from the more spaced houses of medium residential areas, the large flat parking surfaces, the continuous dark green canopy of forests, and the open green lawns of parks.
desert: Desert presents a vast, uniform expanse of light tan or pale yellow sand with subtle wind-formed ripple textures and no vegetation, distinguishing it from the similar but smaller bare soil patches of bareland, the dark green continuous canopy of forests, the smooth sand of beaches, and the dark flowing water of rivers.
farmland: Farmland displays large, regularly gridded patches of crops with distinct linear row patterns, alternating color bands of green and brown, and clear geometric field boundaries, distinguishing it from the uniform green grass of meadows, the flat structures of industrial zones, the smooth water surfaces of ponds, and the large paved areas of airports.
forest: Forest exhibits a dense, continuous dark green canopy with a fine-grained rough clumpy texture showing no geometric structure or regular pattern, distinguishing it from the vast dry tones of desert, the rugged terrain of mountains, the tightly packed rooftops of dense residential areas, and the scattered buildings of sparse residential zones.
industrial: Industrial areas display large rectangular factory buildings with flat rooftops, clusters of circular storage tanks, wide internal roads, and minimal vegetation, distinguishing them from the circular storage tank clusters, the regular crop patterns of farmland, the linear railway tracks of railway stations, the dense commercial buildings, and the expansive parking surfaces.
meadow: A meadow presents a broad, uniform expanse of bright green grass with a smooth fine texture and no visible geometric patterns or structures, distinguishing it from the regular crop row patterns of farmland, the smooth water surfaces of ponds, the rectangular courts of playgrounds, the sinuous water of rivers, and the bare soil of bareland.
mediumresidential: Medium residential areas feature moderately spaced single-family houses with visible yards, a regular street grid, and a balanced mix of rooftops and green space, distinguishing them from the tightly packed rooftops of dense residential areas, the widely scattered houses of sparse residential areas, the developed resort areas, and the large parking surfaces.
mountain: Mountain terrain displays rugged, irregular topography with varied tones of rock and sparse vegetation, showing natural contour patterns and shadow variations from elevation changes, distinguishing it from the continuous dark green canopy of forests, the smooth uniform tones of bareland, the vast dry sand of desert, and the dark flowing water of rivers.
park: A park features large open green lawns with scattered trees, winding paths, and possibly small ponds or recreational facilities, distinguishing it from the smooth water surfaces of ponds, the large paved plazas of squares, the fan-shaped geometry of baseball fields, the rectangular buildings of schools, and the developed resort areas.
parking: A parking lot presents a large flat gray paved surface with a regular grid of thin white parking space lines and scattered small dark vehicle rectangles, distinguishing it from the expansive airport tarmac, the dock infrastructure of ports, the surrounding parking of churches, the dense rooftops of residential areas, and the commercial building clusters.
playground: A playground displays small rectangular or irregularly shaped colorful surfaces with visible sports court markings, running tracks, or play equipment shadows, often adjacent to school buildings, distinguishing it from the rectangular building layouts of schools, the oval structures of stadiums, the fan-shaped baseball fields, the open green of parks, and the elevated structures of viaducts.
pond: A pond appears as a small, enclosed, roughly circular or irregular dark smooth water body surrounded by land, with a clear defined shoreline, distinguishing it from the sinuous flowing ribbon of rivers, the green lawns of parks, the regular crop patterns of farmland, the fan-shaped dirt infields of baseball fields, and the sandy shoreline of beaches.
port: A port contains complex water boundaries with linear dock structures, moored ships appearing as large bright elongated objects, cranes, and extensive paved storage areas, distinguishing it from the large parking surfaces, the factory buildings of industrial zones, the sandy shoreline of beaches, the calm water of resorts, and the flowing water of rivers.
railwaystation: A railway station features multiple parallel linear railway tracks with platforms, adjacent station buildings, and surrounding industrial or commercial structures, distinguishing it from the large factory complexes of industrial zones, the expansive parking areas, the runway strips of airports, the elevated structures of viaducts, and the dense buildings of urban centers.
resort: A resort displays a mix of low-rise buildings with swimming pools, landscaped green areas, and proximity to water bodies or beaches, with a relaxed layout and abundant recreational facilities, distinguishing it from the sandy beaches, the more spaced houses of medium residential areas, the calm water of ponds, the open green of parks, and the dense residential rooftops.
river: A river appears as a sinuous, naturally curving ribbon of dark smooth water with irregular banks and variable width flowing through the landscape, distinguishing it from the enclosed still water of ponds, the linear structures of bridges, the smooth sand of beaches, the vast dry tones of desert, and the continuous green canopy of forests.
school: A school features a large rectangular main building with adjacent rectangular playgrounds or sports courts, open green yards, and surrounding parking areas, distinguishing it from the colorful courts of playgrounds, the large parking surfaces, the open green lawns of parks, the industrial factory buildings, the distinctive spires of churches, and the plazas of squares.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential areas show widely scattered individual houses with abundant surrounding vegetation and large gaps between structures, distinguishing them from the tightly packed rooftops of dense residential areas, the more organized layouts of medium residential areas, the continuous dark green canopy of forests, and the still water of ponds.
square: A square appears as a large, open, flat paved or semi-paved rectangular area surrounded by buildings, with minimal vegetation and clear geometric boundaries, distinguishing it from the green open lawns of parks, the dense building clusters of urban centers, the large parking surfaces, the courts of playgrounds, and the commercial building blocks.
stadium: A stadium displays a large oval or rectangular enclosed structure with tiered seating visible as concentric rings, a central green field, and surrounding parking areas, distinguishing it from the fan-shaped baseball fields, the dense building clusters of urban centers, the colorful courts of playgrounds, the large parking surfaces, and the rectangular buildings of schools.
storagetanks: Storage tanks appear as a cluster of perfectly circular, uniform-sized bright metallic or white cylindrical structures with consistent shadows, typically located within industrial areas, distinguishing them from the large factory buildings of industrial zones, the still water of ponds, the vast dry tones of desert, and the regular crop patterns of farmland.
viaduct: A viaduct appears as a long, elevated linear concrete structure with regular support pillars crossing over terrain or roads, casting rhythmic shadow patterns, distinguishing it from the linear water-crossing structure of bridges, the large flat parking surfaces, the colorful courts of playgrounds, the railway tracks of railway stations, and the dense buildings of urban centers.
